description: CreatorOS mapped against the 13-layer production stack -- current state, target state, gaps, blockers, readiness, risk, and cross-layer dependencies for all 13 layers.
provenance_detail: Synthesized from: phase14_6b_creatoros_current_implementation_truth.json (code-resolved current state across GitHub main, Beast, UMH projection), phase14_6b_creatoros_auth_security_truth.json (broken Passport.js, target Clerk, API security gaps), phase14_6b_creatoros_data_ontology.json (20-table schema, missing tables inventory), phase14_6b_creatoros_content_distribution_canon.json (universal composer, cross-posting, scheduling), phase14_6b_creatoros_automation_ai_canon.json (automation builder, AI utility features, email/newsletter, search), phase14_6b_creatoros_community_messaging_canon.json (communities, DMs, channels), phase14_6b_creatoros_product_types_commerce_canon.json (10 product types, commerce primitives), phase14_6b_creatoros_ugc_ads_canon.json (UGC campaigns, ads platform), phase14_6b_creatoros_design_identity_canon.json (X/Twitter minimalism), phase14_6b_creatoros_source_inventory.json (all source surfaces).
layer_schema_note: This mapping uses the same 13-layer production stack schema as the EOS mapping (Phase 14.6B), re-aligned to application-centric concerns: Frontend Foundations, APIs+Backend, Database+Storage, Auth+Permissions, AI Runtime, Workflow/Automation, Memory/Knowledge, Analytics+Observability, Infrastructure+Deployment, Testing+QA, Documentation, Security+Compliance, Integration+Ecosystem. CreatorOS differs fundamentally from EOS: it is a consumer-facing creator platform (Whop on steroids) rather than an AI-native business operating system. AI is utility-level, not agent-level. The 13 layers apply but the concerns within each layer differ significantly.

current_status.eos_boundary_note: EOS has 10 department agents, 66 skills, full UMH substrate integration, multi-model routing, governance, and autonomous execution. CreatorOS AI is fundamentally different: utility functions that suggest, human decides. No agent hierarchy, no delegation, no authority engine. The only overlap is the AI chatbot product type, and even those are different: EOS agents work FOR the entrepreneur, CreatorOS agents are products creators SELL to consumers.

critical_path.description: Fix broken authentication by migrating to Clerk. This is the single P0 gate that blocks ALL production deployment. Do NOT fix Passport.js -- migrate directly to Clerk. Steps: Clerk project setup, add clerk_id to users table, swap middleware from Passport to Clerk Express SDK, swap frontend auth components to Clerk React, implement webhook sync, audit all routes for protection.
critical_path.note: Unlike EOS which has DEC-145-001 (source divergence) as its gate, CreatorOS has COS-AUTH-001 (broken auth) as its gate. This is a smaller, more tractable blocker.

critical_path.description: Split routes.ts (53KB) into 10-15 domain-specific route modules. Split storage.ts (104KB) into domain-specific storage modules. This unlocks testability, parallel development, and security auditing. Must happen before any feature expansion.

Extend schema for MVP features. Phase 1: add product_type discriminator, scheduled_at/published_at/status on posts, clerk_id on users, community owner FK. Phase 2: add commerce tables (orders, order_items, entitlements). Phase 3: add course, email, automation tables. Provision production Neon database.

Create Dockerfile, Fly.toml, health check endpoint. Set up GitHub Actions CI (lint, type-check, build). Deploy to Fly.io staging. Provision production Neon database. Can start after auth migration is validated.

RLS on user-scoped tables. Rate limiting on all endpoints. Security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options). Input validation middleware. Error handling middleware. Content moderation system (at minimum: reporting + manual review). Privacy policy and ToS. Must complete before accepting real user content.

Responsive layout (desktop sidebar + mobile bottom nav). Missing page implementation starting with highest-value screens: content calendar, product creation/checkout, analytics dashboard, settings. Incremental -- each page depends on its backend route module.

Content suggestion engine (highest creator value). Smart scheduling (statistical spine + LLM explanation). Enhance existing chatbot feature (model selection, streaming, token tracking). Auto-moderation integration with content moderation system.

Install Vitest + Playwright. Write critical path tests: auth flow, content creation, product purchase, community join. CI integration. Should ramp up alongside each layer as decomposed modules are built.
PostHog integration for product analytics. Structured logging. Error tracking. Creator dashboard with engagement metrics. Commerce funnel analytics (after Stripe). Depends on deployment existing.

Visual automation flow editor. Trigger/action execution engine. pg-boss background job queue. Pre-built templates. Deferred past core platform because it requires commerce, email, and community systems to provide meaningful triggers and actions.
Email template system. Course curriculum storage. Document search and organization. AI agent knowledge base. Largely dependent on other systems existing first.

OAuth connections to social platforms (Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest). Cross-posting engine. Content scheduling via platform APIs. This is the 'post once, publish everywhere' promise -- the core differentiator. Deferred because it requires platform developer app approvals (weeks of lead time) and each platform API is a significant integration effort.

readiness_summary.advantage_over_eos: CreatorOS has a significant structural advantage over EOS: NO SOURCE DIVERGENCE. EOS has 401-file divergence between GitHub main (202 files) and Beast (603 files) gated behind DEC-145-001. CreatorOS has a single aligned codebase. This means the critical path is shorter: fix auth -> decompose god files -> extend schema -> deploy. No source convergence required.
readiness_summary.disadvantage_vs_eos: CreatorOS has ZERO tests (EOS has 11 UMH integration tests + 4 unit tests + 97 referenced). CreatorOS god files (routes.ts 53KB, storage.ts 104KB) are worse than EOS (which at least has modular route files on Beast). And the core product promise ('post once, publish everywhere') requires external platform integrations that take weeks of approval time.

primary_blocker: COS-AUTH-001: comparePasswords() returns true for ALL passwords. Authentication is non-functional. This is a CRITICAL P0 vulnerability that blocks all production deployment. Resolution: migrate directly to Clerk (do not fix Passport.js). Unlike EOS where the primary blocker is a decision (DEC-145-001: source divergence), CreatorOS's blocker is a technical fix with a known solution path (Clerk migration). The 3 partially-ready layers (Frontend, Database, AI) can continue development in parallel, but nothing can go to production until auth works.
